text:
A: Right. Hi. Can you hear me?
B: Yeah. Hi. Craig.
A: Gemma. Funny, my husband's called Craig.
B: Lot of us about.
A: Mm. So what is this, we just talk for three minutes and that's it?
B: Pretty much. Did one already. Goes quick.
A: Good. I've been on since six, I'm knackered.
B: What do you do, then?
A: Site ops manager. Distribution centre up near Alconbury, third-party logistics. About a hundred and eighty staff over three shifts. So basically if a trailer doesn't turn up or the agency don't send enough bodies, it's my phone that goes. Had a client on at me at seven this morning about peak volumes. Peak's a nightmare every year, without fail.
B: Huh. I write warehouse software. Logistics company in Cambridge.
A: You're joking.
B: Back-end. The bit that works out allocation, picking routes, that sort of thing.
A: Which one?
B: Probably not one you'd know. Mid-sized.
A: Well, whoever does ours wants shooting. It goes down every time we hit volume. Every time. Two hundred people stood there with scanners going "Gem, it's frozen again."
B: Yeah, that's usually not the software, to be fair.
A: Course it's not.
B: No, honestly. Nine times out of ten someone's set it up badly on site. Waves configured wrong, or the server's some ten-year-old box in a comms cupboard. Then they ring us and it's our fault. Had one last month, their whole system was running off a server someone had put a kettle next to.
A: A kettle.
B: Steam. In the cupboard. For about two years.
A: ...That's actually quite funny. That'd be my lot an' all, to be honest.
B: It's always somebody's lot.
A: Do you go out on site, then, or?
B: God, no. Home, mostly. Office once a fortnight.
A: Must be nice. Sat at home in your joggers.
B: It's alright, yeah.
A: I'd go mad. I'd also never answer an email again, so. My inbox is about four thousand.
B: Four thousand?
A: Ish. My deputy does the important ones, Priya. She's the only reason that place runs, honestly. Don't tell her I said that.
B: I'm not gonna meet her.
A: No. Good. ...Cambridge, though, so you're on the A14?
B: A1(M). Which is a nightmare.
A: Try the A14. The roadworks. I've spent more time sat by Girton this month than I have at home.
B: Yeah, I avoid it.
A: Lucky you. ...Them headphones. You were on a game before this, weren't you?
B: Bit. Lunch break.
A: It's gone four.
B: Flexible hours.
A: Flexible. Right. If one of my team leaders said that to me I'd have them in the office.
B: Good job I don't work for you, then.
A: Yeah, it is, mate. You'd last about a week. My Craig's the same, mind, he's Arsenal, been in a mood since Sunday—
B: Oh, don't. They bottled it agai—
